source.title: Find Beautiful Indices in the Given Array I

teaching.hint: Can the two pattern searches and the distance condition be considered separately?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The definition combines independent occurrence lists with a proximity test on start positions; both lists are naturally sorted.
solution_outline.approach: Find every occurrence start of `a` and `b`. For each `a` start, check whether the ordered `b` starts contain any value in its closed distance window, and retain qualifying starts.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The occurrence lists contain exactly the valid starts for their patterns; each proximity query answers existence in `[i-k,i+k]`.
solution_outline.correctness: A start is returned exactly when it is an `a` occurrence and a `b` start lies in its allowed window. Scanning `a` starts in order preserves sorted output.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(|s|(|a|+|b|)+A log B)` time using ordered lookup for `A,B` occurrence counts, and `O(|s|)` space; pattern lengths are at most 10.
solution_outline.pitfall: Nested comparison of every `a` and `b` occurrence can become quadratic on dense inputs.

common_wrong_turns: Check only b occurrences after i
source_fidelity_notes: The distance applies to start indices, not interval overlap, and equality is permitted.
